pulse: A mixed, chip-led selloff: the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.22% to 27943.74 and the S&P 500 fell 0.40% to 7561.67, while the Dow Jones bucked the trend to close up 0.10% at 52347.55 and the Russell 2000 slipped 0.31% to 2790.49. Breadth was actually positive at 315 advancers versus 185 decliners out of 503 S&P names, but the index-level damage was concentrated in mega-cap tech: Electronic Technology was the weakest sector (-2.11%), dragged by Consumer Durables (-1.51%) and Producer Manufacturing (-1.41%), while Consumer Non-Durables (+1.45%) and Finance (+0.64%) led gainers. The VIX jumped 3.21% to 19.30 on the risk-off tone, the 10-year yield ticked up 0.12% to 5.14%, the dollar (DXY) gained 0.23% to 103.41, WTI crude eased 0.20% to 88.56, and Bitcoin tumbled 3.50% to 65843.84. Among the most-active names, AMD was the standout loser at -8.75% on heavy volume ($26.38B traded), Broadcom fell 4.76% and Micron dropped 2.52%, while Meta rallied 2.90% to buck the chip-sector weakness and Apple and Microsoft held roughly flat.
